message.content:
In a standard Texas Hold’em game each player receives two private cards, so the **maximum number of hearts a single player can hold in their own hand is two**.  
If you include the five community cards that are shared by everyone, a player could theoretically end up with **seven hearts** (their two hole cards plus all five community cards).

So, in any given hand the “player with the highest number of hearts” is simply the player who has the most hearts among all the hands being compared.  
Without knowing the actual cards dealt in a particular game, we can’t point to a specific player—only that the player with the most hearts is the one who holds the greatest number of hearts in that hand.
